newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government-initiated Software Park project, aimed at competing with Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor, has hit a snag after the Budget Bureau rejected the four billion-baht budget allocation for it. The blueprint of the mega-project has been prepared by the Information Technology Development Committee chaired by Prime Minister's Office Minister Sompong Amornvivat. (BANGKOK POST)

- The leadership crisis in Palang Dharma will come to a head later this month when the fractious party meets to elect a new leader. Ahead of the April 27 party congress Palang Dharma is divided into two camps, one supporting its acting leader Chaiwat Sinsuwong for the top post, and the other its former secretary-general Sudarat Keyuraphan who is the party's sole representative in the current parliament. (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung's sons have been involved in the dispute at a bar in Phuket province, an eyewitness and an opposition MP say. Democrat MP for Phuket Anchalee Theppabutr says that there are attempts to intimidate witnesses, particularly those who were named in newspaper reports. The opposition MP says some of the seven witnesses have told her that Chalerm's sons were involved in the brawl and that a shot from a black 11 mm pistol was fired. (THE NATION)

- Thai Danu Bank (TDB) has revealed that its new lending strategy, to be introduced after its merger with Finance One, will focus on the energy sector. TDB Executive Vice-President Sutatt Ramasoot explains that after merging, his bank will have to maintain its existing clientele as well as those of its future partner, many of whom are in the energy sector. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Association of Finance Companies has scheduled a meeting with Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond to ask for more information about measures introduced by the government's property loan management organisation (PLMO). The association's new president, Banterng Tantivit, says the finance sector is somewhat sceptical about how effective the measures will be. (BANGKOK POST)

- Tipco Group of Companies is negotiating a US$600-million asphalt refinery and transport project with the Chinese government to produce five million tonnes of asphalt emulsion annually for road construction throughout China. Group chairman Prasit Supsakorn went to Beijing this week to hold talks with China's transport and deputy transport ministers and other top officials to pursue the project which was proposed by Tipco, Thailand's largest asphalt emulsion maker, during the visit to Beijing by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh from April 2 to 5. (THE NATION)
